data_description.updates_enabled: Scores pending updates as routine, feature, or possibly breaking. Advisory only, never installs anything.
data_description.areas_enabled: Suggests an existing area for each device that has none. Nothing is assigned until you confirm a suggestion in Repairs.
data_description.device_class_enabled: Suggests a device class for sensors that report a unit but have none. Nothing is set until you confirm or pick a class in Repairs.
data_description.config_entries_enabled: Sorts integrations that failed to set up into a passing glitch, a sign-in problem, or broken for good. Advisory only: it never reloads, reconfigures or removes an integration. Its counts include integrations Home Assistant already asks you to sign in to again; Gut Check leaves those to Home Assistant's own card.
data_description.critical_label_enabled: Suggests your critical label for smoke, carbon monoxide and gas sensors, and asks about every valve, switch, siren and moisture sensor to find water shutoffs, leak sensors and sirens. Nothing is labelled until you confirm a suggestion in Repairs, and it does nothing until you pick a critical label.
data_description.daily_budget: A hard stop for the day. It resets at local midnight.
data_description.critical_label: Gut Check never acts on or changes an entity or device with this label. The home health check still watches it and tells you if it goes offline, but every other check leaves it out. Locks, alarms and covers are never checked, label or not.
data_description.change_back: Opens a list of the sensors whose device class Gut Check set, and the sensors it hid, from suggestions you confirmed, so you can change any of them back.
data_description.hide_diagnostic_enabled: Suggests hiding sensors that report on a device or its connection, such as signal strength, network name or storage used, rather than on your home. Nothing is hidden until you confirm a suggestion in Repairs.
data_description.recorder_churn_enabled: Ranks the entities that write to the recorder most often and suggests which could be left out of its history. Advisory only: Gut Check never changes your recorder settings. Each suggestion is a Repairs card with a snippet you add to configuration.yaml yourself.

change_back.title: Change back what Gut Check set
change_back.description: Pick the sensors to change back. Gut Check clears a device class it set or unhides a sensor it hid, leaves any that were changed since, and stops making that suggestion for them.

unavailable_entity.description: `{entity_id}` has been unavailable for {unavailable_for}. Gut Check thinks it is worth fixing. Nothing will be changed automatically, and ignoring this card keeps it hidden on later checks.

possibly_breaking_update.title: Update: {entity_id} may need attention
possibly_breaking_update.description: `{entity_id}` is offering version {latest_version}. Gut Check read the release notes and thinks this update could change or break something. Nothing is installed automatically, and ignoring this card keeps it hidden on later checks.

config_entry_needs_reauth.title: Integration: {title} may need you to sign in again
config_entry_needs_reauth.description: Home Assistant could not set up **{title}** ({integration}). Gut Check read the error it reported and thinks the saved sign-in stopped working. The link below opens the integration's page, where you can sign in again, reconfigure it or remove it. Gut Check never changes an integration itself, and ignoring this card keeps it hidden on later checks.

config_entry_dead.title: Integration: {title} may not work again
config_entry_dead.description: Home Assistant could not set up **{title}** ({integration}). Gut Check read the error it reported and thinks it will not work again as set up, for example because the device or account is gone. The link below opens the integration's page, where you can fix or remove it. Gut Check never changes an integration itself, and ignoring this card keeps it hidden on later checks.

init.description: Gut Check thinks `{entity_id}` guards against fire, gas or water damage, and suggests adding your **{label_name}** label to it. init.title: Suggested: hide this sensor
init.description: Gut Check thinks `{entity_id}` is a diagnostic sensor, one that reports on its device or its connection rather than on your home, and suggests hiding it. A hidden sensor stays off auto-generated dashboards and area pages, so it no longer crowds your temperatures and power readings. It keeps working and recording history. You can unhide it in its entity settings, or change it back from Gut Check's Configure screen. Nothing changes until you choose.

abort.suggestion_outdated: The sensor changed since this suggestion was made, so nothing was changed and the card was removed.
abort.suggestion_ignored: Gut Check will stop suggesting hiding this sensor. The card is now in your ignored repairs.

recorder_exclude_suggestion.title: Recorder: {entity_id} may not need its history
recorder_exclude_suggestion.description:
Gut Check counted how often `{entity_id}` writes a new state to the recorder and rates it **{bucket}** (1,000 to 3,000 changes a day is heavy, 3,000 to 10,000 very heavy, 10,000 or more extreme). It thinks nothing needs this entity's history.

To stop recording it, add it to the `recorder:` section of your configuration.yaml, merging it into any `recorder:` section you already have, then restart Home Assistant:

```yaml
recorder:
  exclude:
    entities:
      - {entity_id}
```

This stops its history and its long-term statistics. The entity keeps working, and automations still see its current state. Gut Check skips the source of a statistics, history stats or filter sensor, but cannot see everything that reads the recorder, such as an SQL sensor. If your recorder section already uses include filters, read the linked page first, because they change how an exclude applies. Gut Check never changes your configuration, and ignoring this card keeps it hidden on later checks.
